precepts.text: A rebellious people who say to the seers, prophesy smooth things, cause the Holy One to cease.
precepts.point: Ahab said there was one man, Micaiah, but he hated him because he never prophesied good, only evil, meaning he told the truth.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

precepts.why:
“That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord: Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” They even say, “cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.”

That is Ahab. Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might enquire of him?” and Ahab answered, there is Micaiah, “but I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil.” Always evil means he told the truth. Ahab wanted smooth things, not right things.

precepts.text: Preach the word in season and out; the time comes when men will not endure sound doctrine.
precepts.point: Ahab said there was one man, Micaiah, but he hated him because he never prophesied good, only evil, meaning he told the truth.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

precepts.why:
“Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.”

“For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.”

That was Ahab. He had heaped to himself prophets that told him what he wanted to hear, and he hated the one man who spoke the truth: “he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil.”

precepts.text: If they speak not according to this word it is because there is no light in them.
precepts.point: Micaiah answered, as the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

precepts.why:
“To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

The messenger told Micaiah, “the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent; let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.” But one assent does not make it true. If they speak not according to the word, there is no light in them, however many there are.

Micaiah answered as a true prophet: “As the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.”

precepts.text: The Most High on his throne asks who shall entice Ahab, and a spirit comes forth and says he will go be a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets, and the Most High sends him to prevail.
precepts.point: A lot of people think the Most High is all hugs and kisses, roses and daisies, but he is loving and he will also lay it to you; the devil, Satan, works for the Most High, and nothing can be done without him allowing it, for they are his.

note.label: Job 12: With God Is Strength and Wisdom

precepts.why:
Micaiah saw “the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left. And the Lord said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came out, stood before the Lord, and said, “I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said, Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do even so.”

The Most High on his throne sends the lying spirit and tells it to prevail. So the deceived and the deceiver are his: the devil, Satan, works for the Most High, and nothing can be done without him allowing it, for they are his. He uses anybody he wants. He breaketh down and it cannot be built again; he shutteth up a man and there can be no opening. He is loving, and he will also lay it to you.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: A quick little history. Remember, very few people are selected and chosen for the Most High’s mission. Christianity has over 400 million followers; everybody and their momma is a Christian. You have MS-13 Christians chopping off heads, selling drugs, killing people in the name of Jesus, kidnapping, extortion, prostitution. Everybody says, ‘I’m a Christian’. But just because you have all those numbers, all those followers, doesn’t mean there is any truth to it.

“Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance”: Jehoshaphat was one of the kings of Judah. “And joined affinity with Ahab”: Ahab was one of the kings of the Northern Kingdom. The Northern Kingdom are the Latino tribes, the Hispanic tribes; Judah is the American Negroes. That’s our identity in the Bible, and now we’re reading the history of what happened.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance”, and “persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth–gilead.” Ahab, king of the Northern Kingdom, was wicked as hell, and he wants Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, who stood with the Lord and was all about the laws and the commandments for the people, to come and join with him. “Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth–gilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people”. Remember, by this time the Northern Kingdom had already split; there was already a division.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.” Before we go to war together, enquire of the Lord. You see who Jehoshaphat’s counsellor was: let’s go to the Lord first.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men”. Four hundred prophets. The kings are sitting on their thrones together, and each prophet comes up and prophesies victory: King Ahab, you shall prosper, you will succeed in your battle. “Shall we go to Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall I forbear?” Should we stop and not go to this war because we’re gonna lose? “And they said, Go up; for God will deliver it into the king’s hand.” Four hundred men prophesied victory for King Ahab.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might enquire of him?” Hold on, hold on. Those are four hundred prophets that said we’re gonna win, but something’s not right here. Is there anybody left besides these four hundred that we can ask?

The kings are set up as kings, but they are not prophets; they go to the prophets. They are kings over the people to have power, they control the army, they control resources, but they are not prophets. There is a difference. King Hezekiah was a king but he was not a prophet; David was a king and a prophet. There is a difference between being a king and being called to be a prophet.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “There is yet one man, by whom we may enquire of the Lord: but I hate him”. Why does he say that? “For he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil”: he never got nothing good to say about me. “The same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.” Wait, Ahab, don’t talk like that; let’s find out, maybe he’s gonna say something good. Four hundred men said y’all are gonna win the war, go forth to battle; why did Jehoshaphat still want to find out if anybody was left? He saw something in the spirit with those men.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.” Each king is sitting on his throne, “clothed in their robes”, “at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.” Zedekiah “had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the Lord, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.” “And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth–gilead, and prosper”.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “And the messenger that went to call Micaiah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent”: all in unison, all in one accord, saying good things to the king. “Let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.” “And Micaiah said, As the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.” I’m only gonna say what the Lord shows to me. That’s how I’m rolling.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: Micaiah comes up and everybody’s looking; remember, Ahab told Jehoshaphat he never says anything good. “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.” “And the king said to him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the Lord?” Tell me the truth: what did you see in the vision? Be honest.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd”. Damn, Micaiah just went against 400 prophets. Micaiah didn’t give a damn; he said the truth. Numbers don’t mean nothing: you stand by the Bible. “And the Lord said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.”

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “Did I not tell thee that he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?” I told you, every time. That’s why he put him in jail. So you had 400 men saying you’re gonna win the war, and only one was telling the truth and spoke the true vision: no, you’re not gonna win, you’re gonna lose. And when you read on, the Lord put a spirit on all those men to prophesy that to the king; that’s what Micaiah was showing him. Then they smacked him in the face and asked which way the Lord went from them to speak to him.

Think about it: all these men saying they’re gonna win the war, and here is Micaiah alone. But Micaiah wasn’t scared. He told the total truth: you’re gonna lose, I don’t care what 400 men said to you, the Lord is going to have you lose. He wasn’t afraid, and that’s how we got to be. Christ said don’t be ashamed to speak of me; if you’re ashamed of me, I’m gonna be ashamed of you before the Father. We don’t want to be that bunch. We want to always stand for the Most High and Christ and his laws. The world has never seen black and Latino men and sisters standing firm for the Bible.
